rfm_tuples.claim_text: Management reports FY2025 net income of $190.3M (vs $35.5M FY24) and characterizes 2025 as a year of 'recently achieved profitability' and 'continued sales growth.' Headline net-income growth implied >5x year-over-year.
rfm_tuples.R: We generated total revenue of $605.5 million and had net income of $190.3 million for the year ended December 31, 2025. We generated total revenue of $441.5 million and had net income of $35.5 million for the year ended December 31, 2024.
rfm_tuples.f_method: earnings_quality — decompose 2025 net income into operating vs one-time tax benefit; reconcile against effective tax rate disclosure
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K Item 7 MD&A + Note 8 Income Taxes + Feb 27 2026 8-K
rfm_tuples.M_value: Of the $190.3M 2025 net income, $103.3M (54%) is a one-time non-cash valuation-allowance release on deferred tax assets, recognized in Q4 2025. Pre-tax income was $107.5M. The effective tax rate was -77.0% (benefit, not provision). Underlying 'core' net income excluding the VA release is ~$87M, only ~2.5x FY24, not 5x. TMDX filed a SECOND 8-K on Feb 27, 2026 (3 days after the 10-K) specifically to clarify the impact of the VA release on previously reported Q4 2025 results — itself a disclosure-quality flag suggesting investor confusion required correction.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B: The headline 'net income up 5x' framing is technically true but quality-of-earnings impaired. Management's own subsequent 8-K (Feb 27) implies they recognized the VA release was being mis-read. The 10-K itself notes 'our income tax rate will increase in the future' — i.e., the optical EPS jump is unrepeatable. For a name down 54%, the issuer's chosen profitability narrative depends on a non-recurring tax item; the underlying operating story is far less favorable.

rfm_tuples.claim_text: TMDX states that as of December 31, 2025, internal control over financial reporting was NOT effective due to a material weakness over inventory movement; PwC issued an ADVERSE opinion on ICFR. Q1/Q2/Q3 2024 and Q1 2025 interim financials had immaterial misstatements as a result.
rfm_tuples.R: we have concluded that our internal control over financial reporting was not effective due to the material weakness... The Company did not design and maintain effective controls over inventory movement within its manufacturing network... The material weakness resulted in immaterial misstatements to inventory, accounts payable, cost of net product revenue, selling, general and administrative expenses and research and development expenses, in the interim consolidated financial statements for the quarterly period ended March 31, 2025 and the quarterly and year-to-date periods ended March 31, 2024, June 30, 2024 and September 30, 2024.
rfm_tuples.f_method: icfr_audit_opinion — confirm material-weakness scope and remediation status across both 10-K (FY25) and Q1 2026 10-Q (Mar 31, 2026)
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K Item 9A + PwC ICFR Opinion + Q1 2026 10-Q Item 4
rfm_tuples.M_value: PwC's audit report explicitly states 'the Company did not maintain... effective internal control over financial reporting as of December 31, 2025'. Q1 2026 10-Q (filed 2026-05-05) confirms material weakness was NOT remediated as of March 31, 2026. Four prior interim periods required correction. Material weakness specifically touches inventory, AP, COGS, SG&A, R&D — i.e., nearly the entire P&L below revenue.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: An ADVERSE ICFR opinion on the most recent 10-K is the strongest accounting-quality red flag the auditor framework allows. Material weakness scope (inventory movement) directly intersects with the short-seller allegations (off-label use, NOP economics) and the securities class-action class period (FY2022-Jan 2025). Inventory at a single-product medical-device manufacturer is the central operating asset. Unremediated through Q1 2026.

The Citizen Petition tail risk is particularly under-priced — FDA suspension of OCS Liver PMA would impair the highest-margin product line; the issuer's own risk-factor explicitly acknowledges even if FDA rejects the petition 'it may nonetheless impact how surgeons, patients and transplant centers perceive the safety and efficacy.'

rfm_tuples.claim_text: Form 4 evidence — CEO Waleed Hassanein executed open-market CODE-P purchases on 2025-08-08 (3 transactions totaling 16,875 shares at $116-$118.68, ~$1.97M) and 2025-11-18 (8,775 shares at $114.00, ~$1.00M). Two purchase events totaling ~$3.0M into the drawdown.
rfm_tuples.f_method: form4 — parse Form 4 XML transaction codes; identify open-market PURCHASES (code P) by C-suite into drawdown; distinguish from grants (code A), exercises (code M), withholding (code F), and 10b5-1 sales (code S)
rfm_tuples.M_source: form4 (EDGAR XML, 23 Form-4 filings 2025-05-29 through 2026-05-22 reviewed in full)
rfm_tuples.M_value: CEO Hassanein bought ~$3M total in two events at $114-$118, AFTER the Jan 2025 short report and AFTER the Feb 2025 class action was filed. Per the framework prompt, this is the 'open-market code-P purchases by C-suite, sized meaningfully, into drawdown' supportive signal — but with three caveats: (a) Both buys came AFTER bad news was already public (not contrarian-against-management-narrative); (b) Sized at ~$3M for a CEO whose total annual compensation/equity is multiples larger — meaningful but not 'all-in'; (c) Stock has since declined another 50%+ from Hassanein's purchase price (cutoff drawdown -54% implies a current price ~$60-$70 vs his $114-$118 buy), so his prior commitment-signal has been substantially impaired by subsequent disclosures. NO other officer or director made open-market purchases in the trailing 12 months. EVERY other officer-level Form 4 was a sale (code S) or option exercise immediately sold (M/S/M combination). CFO Hernandez: code S only ($375 + $1,324 + $5,912 sale legs Mar 4 2026; $920 sale Dec 5 2025). New CCO Cecere: A-only grants Feb 20 2026. GC Forsyth: A-only grant May 21 2026. Tamer Khayal (CMO) adopted a Rule 10b5-1 SALE plan Dec 11 2025 for 22,928 shares to commence Mar 16 2026 — i.e., the CMO put a SELLING plan in place 1 week before year-end and after his own December-quarter equity events. Director Khayal-equivalent (Weill, Lovell, Basile, Ranganath) all used M/S/M exercise-and-sell.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode-B-mixed: The CEO's Code-P buys are the only supportive insider signal in the entire 23-Form-4 dataset. They DO qualify under the framework's escalation rule, but the asymmetry with the rest of the C-suite is the dispositive insight — CFO selling, CMO adopting a 10b5-1 sale plan, GC and CCO receiving grants only with no offsetting purchases, all directors using M/S/M same-day exercise-and-sell. The CEO is alone in personal-balance-sheet conviction, and even his commitment is now substantially underwater. This is NOT a uniform 'management buying together into distress' signal; it is one founder/CEO buying while the rest of the team monetizes.

rfm_tuples.claim_text: Q1 2026 results (10-Q filed 2026-05-05) show revenue $173.9M (+21% YoY vs $143.5M Q1 25), but net income $7.3M vs $25.7M prior-year quarter (-72% YoY) and operating income $13.3M vs $27.4M (-52% YoY). Interest expense doubled to $7.2M; SG&A jumped 44% to $63.0M. Diluted EPS $0.21 vs $0.76 (-72%).
rfm_tuples.R: Total revenue 173,933 ... 143,537 ... Income from operations 13,297 ... 27,443 ... Net income $ 7,315 ... $ 25,682 ... Net income per share Basic $ 0.21 ... $ 0.76
rfm_tuples.f_method: growth_decel — compare Q1 2026 YoY growth rate to FY2025 YoY growth rate; reconcile operating margin trajectory with the issuer's growth narrative
rfm_tuples.M_source: Q1 2026 10-Q condensed consolidated statements of operations
rfm_tuples.M_value: Revenue growth deceleration: FY2025 grew +37% YoY ($605M vs $441M); Q1 2026 grew only +21% YoY. That is a 16 percentage point sequential deceleration in growth rate IN A SINGLE QUARTER. Concurrent operating-margin compression: FY25 operating margin 17.9% → Q1 26 operating margin 7.6% (-1030 bps in one quarter). Drivers: SG&A +44% YoY ($63.0M vs $43.6M, including the independent-review legal costs and continued aircraft/NOP build-out) and R&D +45% ($24.9M vs $17.2M). Interest expense doubled because of convertible-note seasoning and aircraft financing.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode A pass on disclosure (10-Q honestly reports the numbers). Mode B: The combined growth-deceleration + margin-compression pattern is the canonical setup for a multi-quarter guide-down. TMDX gave no formal FY26 guidance in the 10-K, and the Q1 print shows the operating leverage thesis is reversing as the company spends ahead of revenue. Stock-based comp was $30.8M in FY25 (~5% of revenue); R&D and SG&A are scaling faster than revenue. The -54% drawdown likely already reflects part of this, but Q1's -72% net income decline against +21% revenue growth indicates the bear-case operating story is materializing in the income statement.

rfm_tuples.claim_text: Competitive landscape disclosure: 'We are aware of only two other companies providing warm perfusion systems, OrganOx Limited, which was acquired by Terumo Corporation in October 2025, and XVIVO Perfusion AB.' Paragonix was acquired by Getinge in September 2024.
rfm_tuples.R: OrganOx Limited, which was acquired by Terumo Corporation in October 2025, and XVIVO Perfusion AB... We also compete with other cold preservation devices in this industry, such as those from Paragonix Technologies, Inc., which was acquired by Getinge in September 2024.
rfm_tuples.f_method: competitor_capital_event — Mode B: two of TMDX's three main competitors were recently acquired by global multi-billion-dollar medical-device strategics. What does that imply for competitive pressure?
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K Competition section + Mode-B inference (no external query)
rfm_tuples.M_value: TMDX's two highest-profile competitors are now subsidiaries of Terumo (Tokyo, ~$15B market cap, global cardiology/transfusion footprint) and Getinge (Stockholm, ~$5B, surgical/critical-care). Both acquirers have hundreds of existing transplant-center relationships, large field sales forces, and bundled-procurement leverage. OrganOx's liver perfusion system directly competes with TMDX's OCS Liver — TMDX's highest-margin product line. The competitive narrative in the 10-K is a single descriptive paragraph; the implications for pricing, GPO contracting, and surgeon-adoption velocity are not discussed.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B: TMDX is the smallest, most-leveraged, most-litigation-exposed player in a 3-competitor warm-perfusion oligopoly that just had 67% of competitive supply consolidate under deep-pocketed strategics in 15 months. The 10-K acknowledges the M&A facts but does not address the implications. Combined with the short-seller-petitioned PMA suspension risk on OCS Liver (the product OrganOx directly competes with), the asymmetric competitive setup is materially under-disclosed.

rfm_tuples.claim_text: Capital structure: $460M 1.50% convertible notes due 2028 (initial conversion price $94.00/share); $60M CIBC term loan at 5.7% variable rate; capped calls cap price $141.88/share. Cash $461.7M at March 31, 2026.
rfm_tuples.R: we entered into a credit agreement with Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce, or CIBC, under which we borrowed $60.0 million. In May 2023, we issued and sold $460.0 million in aggregate principal amount of our Notes... The initial conversion rate is 10.6388 shares of common stock per $1,000 principal amount of the Notes, which represents an initial conversion price of approximately $94.00 per share... cash of $461.7 million as of March 31, 2026 will be sufficient to fund its operations... for at least the next 12 months
rfm_tuples.f_method: convertible_solvency_check — at cutoff price (~$60-$70/share based on -54% drawdown from prior peak), assess refinancing/dilution risk of the 2028 notes
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K Note 7 Long-Term Debt + 10-Q Note on Notes + cash balance
rfm_tuples.M_value: Cash $461.7M vs $460M convertible principal due 2028 — essentially fully cash-covered at maturity if needed, BUT note holders may elect cash or stock settlement (TMDX's option). At a current stock price implied by -54% drawdown (~$60-$70), the converts are well out-of-the-money (conversion price $94) so dilution risk at conversion is low, but ALSO no equity-financing optionality — TMDX cannot easily raise stock at these levels without major dilution. June 8 2026 redemption call right activates immediately after cutoff but only triggers at 130% of $94 ($122.20). The capped call cap price ($141.88) is approximately 2x the current stock price — capped calls are deeply out-of-the-money and provide no economic protection at these levels. Going concern is not at issue, BUT the cash-vs-converts coverage means there is no real refinancing buffer; if operating cash flow deteriorates (Q1 2026 net income $7M, down from $26M), the cash cushion erodes against the 2028 maturity.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode A pass on liquidity disclosure (cash adequate for 12+ months per management; converts cash-covered). Mode B caveat: the convertible structure means no near-term solvency event, but the company has effectively no equity-raise optionality at current prices, the capped calls are economically worthless at these levels, and the converts mature in May 2028 — meaning ~24 months from cutoff to either refinance or pay down. Combined with operating-margin compression and litigation/regulatory tails, this is a name with constrained financial flexibility into a critical 2026-2028 period.

The plan-amendment dissent is the focal proxy signal: shareholders are willing to elect the slate and endorse current pay, but are objecting to additional share-pool dilution at the current valuation. Combined with the CMO's 10b5-1 sale plan and the absence of officer-level open-market buys, the proxy signal corroborates the broader 'C-suite extraction, single CEO conviction' pattern.

supplemental_signals.honesty_alpha_framing: Per Signal OS honesty-alpha memory: TMDX honestly disclosed the material weakness (Sev-1 finding), the class action (Sev-1), the Q1 deceleration (Mode-A truthful), the VA-release earnings-quality issue (Sev-1 with Feb 27 clarifying 8-K), and the activist short-seller petition (Sev-1). Re-detecting honestly disclosed bad news isn't alpha. The honest-alpha contribution here is twofold: (1) the COMPOSITION of risk — material weakness + active 10b-5 litigation + pending FDA Citizen Petition + competitor consolidation — is unusually multi-vector for a non-distressed name with $461M cash; (2) the Form-4 evidence is INTERNALLY DIVERGENT (Hassanein alone in buying vs all other officers/directors distributing), which means the management-commitment signal is partial. The CEO buys partially redeem the score but cannot offset the auditor opinion + litigation/regulatory tail.

summary: TMDX is a complex Mode-A-honest, Mode-B-corroborated SHORT-LEANING NEUTRAL. The 10-K honestly discloses an ADVERSE ICFR opinion (material weakness on inventory movement, unremediated through Q1 2026), a 10b-5 class action with MTD pending, an active FDA Citizen Petition seeking to revoke OCS Liver PMA approval, and FY25 net income inflated by a $103M non-recurring tax-VA release (Feb 27, 2026 8-K issued specifically to clarify the optical EPS jump). Q1 2026 shows growth deceleration to +21% (vs FY25 +37%) and -72% net-income YoY decline (operating margin -1030 bps). Two of three warm-perfusion competitors acquired by Terumo/Getinge in 15 months. Form-4 evidence is mixed: CEO Hassanein executed ~$3M of open-market code-P PURCHASES in Aug 2025 ($1.98M @ $116-118.68) and Nov 2025 ($1.0M @ $114.00) — the only open-market buying in the trailing 12 months. However, every other officer/director with a discretionary transaction either sold (code S, M/S/M exercise-and-sell, or F+S) or adopted a 10b5-1 sale plan (CMO Khayal, Dec 11 2025, 22,928 shares); the May 22 2026 director Form 4 cluster (7 directors, 2,922 shares each) is annual A-coded RSU grants, not buys. Shareholder vote on stock-plan amendment got 28% against — institutional pushback on further dilution. Cash $461.7M is adequate vs $460M 2028 convertibles. Verdict: SHORT-tier on the auditor-opinion + litigation + regulatory + Q1-deceleration vector; the CEO's open-market commitment is the lone supportive signal but is itself underwater (purchases at $114-$118 now ~50% below water at cutoff). Severity counts: P=1, M=4, S=3, R=0, U=1. Composite: 0.30 (distressed but not collapse-tier — CEO commitment is the floor).
